question: Let $\vec{a}=2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+6\hat{k}$.(a) Find the unit vector in the direction of $\vec{a}$.(b) Obtain a vector of magnitude $21$ in the direction opposite to $\vec{a}$.(c) Verify the magnitude of the vector obtained in part (b).
explanation: (a)The magnitude of $\vec{a}$ is`|\vec{a}|=\sqrt{2^2+(-3)^2+6^2}=\sqrt{49}=7`Therefore, the unit vector in the direction of $\vec{a}$ is`\hat{a}=\frac{\vec{a}}{|\vec{a}|}=\frac{1}{7}(2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+6\hat{k})\hat{a}=\frac{2}{7}\hat{i}-\frac{3}{7}\hat{j}+\frac{6}{7}\hat{k}`(b)The unit vector opposite to the direction of $\vec{a}$ is $-\hat{a}$. Therefore, the required vector is`\vec{b}=21(-\hat{a})\vec{b}=-21\left(\frac{2}{7}\hat{i}-\frac{3}{7}\hat{j}+\frac{6}{7}\hat{k}\right)\vec{b}=-6\hat{i}+9\hat{j}-18\hat{k}`(c)`|\vec{b}|=\sqrt{(-6)^2+9^2+(-18)^2}|\vec{b}|=\sqrt{36+81+324}=\sqrt{441}=21`Final ResultThe vector $-6\hat{i}+9\hat{j}-18\hat{k}$ has magnitude $21$ and is directed opposite to $\vec{a}$.

options.C:
(a) $\frac{2}{7}\hat{i}-\frac{3}{7}\hat{j}+\frac{6}{7}\hat{k}$
(b) $6\hat{i}-9\hat{j}+18\hat{k}$
(c) Its magnitude is $21$, but it has the same direction as $\vec{a}$.
